This guide is for engineers who are working on {project-display-name}

toc::[]

PRs are always welcome!

For details on the V4 Pact specification, refer to https://github.com/pact-foundation/pact-specification/tree/version-4

For details on the Pact plugin framework, refer to https://github.com/pact-foundation/pact-plugins

== Raising defects

Before raising an issue, make sure you have checked the open and closed issues to see if an answer is provided there.
There may also be an answer to your question on https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/pact[stackoverflow].

Please provide the following information with your issue to enable us to respond as quickly as possible.

. The relevant versions of the packages you are using (plugin and Pact versions).
. The steps to recreate your issue.
. An executable code example where possible.

=== New features / changes

. Fork it
. Create your feature branch (git checkout -b my-new-feature)
. Commit your changes (git commit -am 'feat: Add some feature')
. Push to the branch (git push origin my-new-feature)
. Create new Pull Request

==== Commit messages

We follow the https://github.com/bcoe/conventional-changelog-standard/blob/master/convention.md[Conventional Changelog]
message conventions. Please ensure you follow the guidelines.

Rust changes use `feat(rust):` / `fix(rust):`. Breaking changes append `!`.

=== Building the plugin

The plugin is written in Rust. Building it needs the toolchain pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`.

[source,shell]
----
cargo build --release
bash scripts/pluginLocalInstall.sh
----

`scripts/pluginLocalInstall.sh` copies the binary and the plugin manifest into the Pact plugin directory. See the installation instructions on {doc-url}.

=== Running the tests

.Unit tests
[source,shell]
----
cargo test --locked
----

Golden and schema fixtures under `tests/fixtures` change only in a commit whose message states why the behavior changed.

Build and install the plugin first (see "Building the plugin" above), then:

.Consumer and provider e2e tests
[source,shell]
----
cargo test --test e2e_consumer --test e2e_provider -- --include-ignored
----

=== Releasing

Releases are cut by running the "Prepare release" workflow. It computes the next version from Conventional Commit subjects since the last tag and opens a `chore: bump version -> X.Y.Z` pull request as the `hominux-automation` GitHub App (org secrets `AUTOMATION_APP_CLIENT_ID` and `AUTOMATION_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`), so the PR triggers CI workflows, whose author-guarded jobs are skipped, and a maintainer can approve it.
Only a maintainer (admin or maintain role) can run "Prepare release". Squash- or rebase-merge the pull request: a merge commit does not match the release trigger. The merge runs "Release" with no further approval: it tags and publishes. Running "Release" by hand is always a dry run.
If a release run fails after the tag is pushed, re-run the failed jobs: tagging reuses a tag that points at the same commit, and the plan job skips a version only once its GitHub release exists. If the post-publish smoke test fails, fix on `main` and cut a patch release; never delete or move a published tag or release.
After the smoke test passes, the run opens a pull request against https://github.com/pact-foundation/pact-plugins[pact-foundation/pact-plugins] that adds the version to its plugin index; until that merges, `pact-plugin-cli install avro` does not see the release.
The `PACT_PLUGINS_PR_TOKEN` secret (a fine-grained token for your pact-plugins fork) lives in the `release` environment. The `preflight` job fails a real run when it is missing, before anything is tagged. To retry only the index pull request, run `GH_TOKEN=<token> bash scripts/index-pr.sh vX.Y.Z`.
CI skips the bump pull request: each PR-triggered job carries an `if:` guard on the PR author. A job-level skip reports as passing, so required checks stay satisfied; `[skip ci]` would leave them pending.
